name: PERU
lead: Peru has snowy Andes mountains, steamy Amazon jungle and a cool desert coast. The Inca built stone cities without any glue between the stones, and Machu Picchu still perches on its misty mountaintop. Peru has the world's highest lake for big ships.
geo: Peru has three lands side by side. The Pacific coast is desert, drier than the Sahara in places. Peaks over 6,000 m wear snow in the Andes.
East of the Andes, jungle covers more than half the country. Lake Titicaca sits at 3,812 m, so high the air feels thin.
animals: Alpacas graze on Andean grasslands. Their soft wool has made clothes for thousands of years. The giant condor rides warm air on wings 3.2 m wide.
Pink river dolphins swim through the flooded Amazon forest. The cock-of-the-rock, Peru's national bird, is bright orange and dances to win a mate.
culture: Ceviche, raw fish soaked in lime juice with chilli, is the national dish. Peru gave the world the potato, and over 3,000 kinds still grow here.
At Inti Raymi in Cusco each June, on the shortest day, people honour the Inca sun god in dazzling costumes. Panpipes and the tiny charango guitar give the highlands their sound.
history: Around the year 1400, the Inca built the biggest empire the Americas had seen, 4,000 km from Colombia to Chile. They moved huge stones without wheels.
Spanish conquerors arrived in 1532, and the Inca Empire collapsed within a decade. Peru became independent in 1821, declared by General José de San Martín.
wows: Outside Peru, Machu Picchu stayed unknown for 400 years until 1911, though local farmers knew it.
Peru has over 1,800 bird species, about one in five on Earth.
The Nazca Lines are giant desert drawings, 2,000 years old and only visible from the air.
Over 5,000 kinds of potato come from wild Andean plants.
Colca Canyon is 3,400 m deep, twice as deep as America's Grand Canyon.
The Amazon River begins as melted snow in the Peruvian Andes.
Inca stones fit so tightly that paper cannot slide between them.

myths.myth: Machu Picchu was the Inca capital
myths.fact: It was a royal retreat for Emperor Pachacuti. Cusco was the capital.

myths.myth: The Inca had no way to keep records
myths.fact: They used knotted strings called quipu. The knots stored numbers.
